newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's white right decries de Kock sentence.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's white right decries de Kock sentence.

text.p: The right-wing white Conservative Party said on Thursday the jail sentence imposed on apartheid killer Eugene de Kock was possibly the heaviest ever handed down in South Africa and condemned it as too severe.
A court on Wednesday gave de Kock two life sentences and an additional 212 years for six murders and more than 80 other crimes committed while he was a security police colonel.

"Such a punishment is completely out of proportion and is apparently the heaviest imposed in a South African court for any offence," the party, which stands for separate rule for Afrikaners, said in a statement.
South Africa still has the death penalty on its law books but it has not been carried out since 1990. Earlier this year it was declared unconstitutional.
The party said it was unacceptable that former members of the security forces were being tried for apartheid era crimes while their opponents in the liberation groups were not prosecuted.

"We are dealing here with a regime that condones its own brutal murders," the statement said, citing a bomb placed by African National Congress guerrillas outside air force headquarters in Pretoria in the 1980s which killed several civilians.
ANC leaders have said they see no necessity to seek amnesty for the bombing or other actions they describe as part of a legitimate armed struggle against apartheid.
